title.narrative: Core Support to Indep Asso Broadcasters
Core Support to Indep Asso Broadcasters

description.narrative: This is one of the core-supported NGOs, funded to improve their institutional systems and to continue their mission-based activities over 2014-2017.

Objective of the intervention: To support systemic organisational improvements in the Independent Association of Broadcaster to establish a healthy and transparent mission-based organisation. IAB's Vision for 2015-2018: The institutional capacity of independent audio-visual content producers and distributors has been improved and the regulatory pressure on them has been decreased IAB's mission: 1. Protection of freedom of speech --> 2. Free media market development --> 3. promoting prosperity of IAB members

The support to IAB was provided in the form of core support with the aim at providing ownership (IAB implements their own strategies) and sustainability (a considerable advance in systemic improvements, financial management, anticorruption and procurement policies). The activities of the organization were focused on the following six strategic projects with corresponding goals to ensure the achievement of a common 2019 vision: 1) Television and radio broadcasting market deregulation; 2) Strengthening IAB members; 3) Education; 4) Social impact; 5) Supporting the East and Crimea; 6) Organisational development.
IAB managed to ensure relative stability within the regulatory field where independent media and national content producers operate. Despite a large number of legislative initiatives, there was no excessive expansion of the powers of regulatory authorities, especially regarding content regulation. The objections of IAB and other organizations concerning the danger of the introduction of increased control over the media were taken into account by lawmakers. At the same time, IAB managed to develop and promote the idea of co-regulation, which can greatly reduce the risks of censorship. No broadcasters ceased operations during the reporting period because of the digital reform. IAB did not manage to significantly expand opportunities for the development of media and new modern forms of monetization because the basic legislation on media and advertising was not revised during the period.
Thanks to a series of successful co-production projects and innovative approaches to content production, the Association was able to significantly increase the ability of several dozen of regional broadcasters to cooperate and co-produce.
IAB education programs improved media specialists professional skills, which has contributed to more effective operation and audience growth of the media companies. In 2016-2019, 151 media specialist took part in IAB education programs.
IAB annual Honor of Profession contest increased its popularity and was highly supported by the professional community of journalists.
In 2016-2019, IAB organized 4 Honor of Profession contests acknowledging quality journalism and best practices of Ukraines media. The contests traditionally included 6 key nominations: Best Interview, Best News Coverage of Resonant Event, Best Opinion-Based Journalism, Best Analytics, Best Investigation, Best Journalistic Report and some special nominations as well as special prizes.
In 2016, IAB conducted the Broadcasting Strategies for Donbass conference (in Kramatorsk). 109 participants attended the conference. As a result, the concept of broadcasting strategy for Donbass was developed, briefings for the commandants of the cities close to ATO zone were initiated, and the unified rules for the arrangements of journalists' work in combat operational zones were initiated.
IAB managed to show significant progress according to the main organizational development indicators (from 3.83 to 4.21 out of 5), including strengthening of: financial viability; service delivery; productive partnerships and collaborations; strategic outreach and branding; sectoral leadership.
Internally, IAB has improved (from 3.83 to 4.43) its governance, mission and strategic management; practices and systems; human resources; financial systems and adaptive capacity. All the recommendations from system-based audit were implemented during the core support period.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
